hindi: देहधारियों के सिर में और हृदय में कितने रोग कहे गए हैं? और अनिल आदि के मान के विकल्प से उत्पन्न होने वाले रोग भी कितने हैं?
english: How many diseases are declared in the head and in the heart of embodied beings? And how many diseases of Vāta (anila) and the others are born of variation in measure?
notes: The question begins here and runs to unit 4; the questioner is named Hutāśaveśa in unit 5. māna-vikalpa ('variation in measure') refers to the doṣas being in different degrees; the answer is in units 6 and 41-42.

hindi: हे निष्पाप! कितने क्षय बताए गए हैं, और कितनी पिडकाएँ? और हे दोषों का नाश करने वाले! दोषों की गति कितने प्रकार की कही गई है?
english: How many depletions (kṣaya) are enumerated, and how many boils (piḍakā), O sinless one? And of how many kinds is the course of the doṣas stated to be, O destroyer of doṣas?

text_flags.why: anaga is not a fitting vocative here; anagha 'O sinless one' is the usual address, with only the aspiration lost; the syllable count is unchanged

notes: Both vocatives (anagha, doṣasūdana) are epithets of the teacher addressed; the line does not name him.

words.gloss: born of variation in the measure of the doṣas

english: Five head diseases are recognised, and five heart diseases; of diseases born of variation in the measure of the doṣas there are sixty plus two.

english: There are ten and eight depletions (kṣaya), seven boils (piḍakā) relating to madhumeha, and the course of the doṣas is stated to be threefold. Hear (them) in detail.
notes: daśa aṣṭau ca = eighteen. madhumeha is kept as the Sanskrit disease name.

lines_iast: daśāṣṭau ca kṣayāḥ sapta piḍakā mādhumehikāḥ

hindi: रोकने से, दिन में सोने से, रात में जागने से, मद से, ऊँचे स्वर में बोलने से, ओस से, पूर्व की वायु से, अति मैथुन से,
english: From suppression (of urges), from day-sleep, from keeping awake at night, from intoxication, from loud speaking, from dew, from the east wind, from excessive intercourse,
notes: The list of causes runs through units 8-10; the verb is in unit 11. saṃdhāraṇa ('holding back') is read as suppression of natural urges; the object is not stated in the line.

words.gloss: from dust, smoke, snow and sun
from taking heavy, sour and green (food)

hindi: असात्म्य गन्ध के सूँघने से, धूल, धुएँ, हिम और धूप से, भारी, खट्टे और हरित पदार्थों के ग्रहण से, अति शीतल जल के सेवन से,
english: from smelling an unsuitable smell, from dust, smoke, snow and sun, from taking heavy, sour and green (food), from use of very cold water,
notes: ati is printed as a separate word before śītāmbusevanāt; it is read with it ('very cold water' or 'excessive use of cold water'). harita 'green' is read as green herbs or vegetables. gandhād asātmyād āghrātāt: 'from an unsuitable smell (that is) smelled'. ati may also be read with the preceding ādānāt ('from excessive taking of heavy, sour and green food').

words.gloss: from reversal of place and time

hindi: सिर पर आघात से, दूषित आम से, रोने से, आँसुओं को रोकने से, मेघों के आने से, मन के सन्ताप से, देश और काल की विपरीतता से,
english: from injury to the head, from vitiated āma, from weeping, from suppression of tears, from the coming of clouds, from mental distress, from reversal of place and time,

text_flags.why: possible: vāṣpa is a b/v spelling variant of bāṣpa 'tears', which unit 17 prints as bāṣpa; sense unchanged

notes: āma (undigested matter) is kept as Sanskrit. deśakālaviparyaya: unwholesome reversal of the normal character of place and season.

hindi: वात आदि सिर में कुपित हो जाते हैं और रक्त दूषित हो जाता है; तब सिर में विविध लक्षणों वाले रोग उत्पन्न होते हैं।
english: Vāta and the others are aggravated in the head and the blood is vitiated; then diseases of various signs arise in the head.
notes: Main clause for the ablatives of units 8-10.

hindi: जहाँ प्राणधारियों के प्राण और सब इन्द्रियाँ आश्रित हैं, और जो अंगों में उत्तम अंग है, वह सिर कहलाता है।
english: That in which the vital breaths (prāṇa) of living beings and all the senses are lodged, and which is the highest of the limbs, is called the head.
lines_deva: प्राणाः प्राणभृतां यत्र श्रिताः सर्वेन्द्रियाणि च
lines_iast: prāṇāḥ prāṇabhṛtāṃ yatra śritāḥ sarvendriyāṇi ca

words.gloss: pratiśyā, diseases of mouth, nose, eyes and ears, and giddiness of the head
words.gram: m. nom. pl., dvandva (with tat-puruṣa members)

hindi: अर्धावभेदक हो सकता है, या पूरा सिर दुखता है; प्रतिश्या, मुख, नाक, आँख और कान के रोग, सिर का चकराना,
english: There may be ardhāvabhedaka, or the whole head aches; pratiśyā, diseases of the mouth, nose, eyes and ears, giddiness of the head,
notes: The list continues into unit 14. ardhāvabhedaka and pratiśyā are kept as Sanskrit disease names.
lines_deva: अर्धावभेदको वा स्यात् सर्वं वा रुज्यते शिरः
lines_iast: ardhāvabhedako vā syāt sarvaṃ vā rujyate śiraḥ

words.gloss: stiffness of throat, manyā and jaw
words.gram: m. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa with dvandva

words.gloss: arising from Vāta etc. and from worms

hindi: अर्दित, सिर का काँपना, गले, मन्या और हनु की जकड़न, और वात आदि तथा कृमियों से उत्पन्न होने वाले अन्य विविध रोग।
english: ardita, tremor of the head, stiffness of the throat, the manyā (neck) and the jaw, and various other diseases arising from Vāta and the others and from worms.
notes: Continues the list of unit 13; the sense is that these occur in the head. ardita kept as Sanskrit; manyā is the side of the neck.

hindi: परन्तु संग्रह में परम ऋषियों ने जिन पाँच शिरोरोगों को अलग-अलग बताया है, उन्हें उनके अपने-अपने हेतुओं और लक्षणों के साथ मुझसे सुनो।
english: But the five head diseases which have been indicated separately in the summary by the supreme sages, hear those from me with their respective causes and signs.
notes: saṃgraha 'summary' refers to the brief listing (cf. unit 6, 'five head diseases'). hetulakṣaṇa as a dvandva takes the gender of lakṣaṇa (n.).

words.gloss: from loud speaking and excessive speaking

hindi: ऊँचे स्वर में बोलने और अधिक बोलने से, तीक्ष्ण पान से, जागरण से, शीतल वायु के स्पर्श से, मैथुन से, वेगों को रोकने से,
english: From loud speaking and excessive speaking, from sharp drinks, from keeping awake, from contact with cold wind, from sexual intercourse, from suppression of urges,
notes: The causes of Vāta head disease run through units 16-17; the verb is in unit 18. māruta here is physical wind (glossary: physical wind = wind). tīkṣṇapāna: drinking of sharp (strong) drinks.

words.gloss: from tears, grief, fear and fright
from loads, travel and excessive emaciation

hindi: उपवास से, आघात से, अति विरेचन और वमन से, आँसू, शोक, भय और त्रास से, भार, मार्ग-गमन और अति कृशता से,
english: from fasting, from injury, from purgation and emesis in excess, from tears, grief, fear and fright, from (carrying) loads, from travel and from excessive reducing,
notes: abhīghāta is a lengthened form of abhighāta 'injury'. ati at the end of the first line is read with virekād vamanād ('in excess'). bhāra-mārga-atikarśana may also be read 'excessive emaciation from loads and travel'.

hindi: बढ़ी हुई वायु सिर में स्थित सिराओं में प्रवेश करके कुपित होती है; तब उसको वात से बड़ा शूल उत्पन्न होता है।
english: Increased Vāta (vāyu), having entered the vessels (sirā) situated in the head, is aggravated; then from Vāta great pain (śūla) arises for him.
notes: Main clause for the ablatives of units 16-17. śirogatāḥ sirāḥ are taken as f. acc. pl., object of āviśya.

words.gloss: together with the middle of the brows

hindi: दोनों शंख बहुत चुभते हैं, और घाटा भी फटती है; भौंहों के मध्य सहित ललाट, अत्यन्त वेदना से युक्त होकर, मानो जलता है।
english: The two temples (śaṅkha) are intensely pricked, and the nape (ghāṭā) likewise is split; and the forehead together with the middle of the brows, with excessive pain, burns as it were.
notes: Signs of Vāta head disease run through units 19-21.
lines_deva: निस्तुद्येते भृशं शङ्खौ घाटा संभिद्यते तथा

hindi: दोनों कान ध्वनि से आहत होते हैं; दोनों आँखें मानो बाहर खींची जाती हैं; पूरा सिर मानो घूमता है और मानो जोड़ों से छूट जाता है।
english: The two ears are struck with sound; the two eyes are as if pulled out; the whole head as if whirls and is as if loosened from its joints.
notes: vadhyete is read as passive of √vadh 'strike'; svanataḥ is read as svana + -tas 'with sound' (a participle agreeing with the neuter dual śrotre would be svanatī).

lines_iast: ghūrṇatīva śiraḥ sarvaṃ saṃdhibhya iva mucyate

english: The network of vessels throbs excessively and the neck is stiffened; and in head disease of Vāta (anila) nature what is unctuous and hot gives relief.
notes: upaśete: 'is suitable, gives relief' (upaśaya).

words.gloss: by pungent, sour, salty, alkali, wine, anger, sun and fire

english: By pungent, sour, salty (things), alkali (kṣāra), wine, anger, sun and fire, Pitta vitiated in the head leads to head disease.

hindi: उससे सिर जलता है और दुखता है, शीत …; दोनों आँखें जलती हैं; प्यास, भ्रम और स्वेद उत्पन्न होते हैं।
english: By it the head burns and aches; cold …; the two eyes burn; thirst, giddiness and sweating arise.

words.gloss: by heavy, unctuous food and over-eating

hindi: बैठे रहने के सुखों से, सोने के सुखों से, भारी और स्निग्ध भोजन तथा अति भोजन से सिर में दूषित श्लेष्मा शिरोरोग उत्पन्न करता है।
english: By the pleasures of sitting, by the pleasures of sleep, by heavy and unctuous food and by over-eating, Kapha (śleṣman) vitiated in the head leads to head disease.

text_flags.why: typing error: the vowel e is missing (Devanagari श्ल्ष्मा); śleṣmā is required by sense and by the syllable count of the line

notes: guru-snigdha-ati-bhojanaiḥ may also be read 'by excessive eating of heavy and unctuous (food)'.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., dvandva used as adj.

hindi: उससे सिर मन्द पीड़ा वाला, सुन्न, स्तिमित और भारी हो जाता है; तन्द्रा उत्पन्न होती है, तथा आलस्य और अरोचक भी।
english: By it the head becomes of mild pain, numb, stiff and heavy; drowsiness arises, likewise lassitude and loss of taste (arocaka).

hindi: त्रिदोषज शिरोरोग में वात से शूल, भ्रम और कम्प; पित्त से दाह, मद और प्यास; कफ से भारीपन और तन्द्रा होती है।
english: In head disease born of the three doṣas: from Vāta, pain (śūla), giddiness and tremor; from Pitta, burning, intoxication (mada) and thirst; from Kapha, heaviness and drowsiness.

words.gloss: from eating sesame, milk, jaggery, (food) undigested, putrid and mixed

hindi: तिल, दूध, गुड़, अजीर्ण में, सड़े हुए और संकीर्ण भोजन से, दोषों से भरे हुए मनुष्य के रक्त, कफ और मांस का क्लेद उत्पन्न होता है।
english: From eating sesame, milk and jaggery (guḍa), (eating) while undigested, and putrid and mixed food, excess moisture (kleda) of the blood, Kapha and flesh arises in one abounding in doṣas.
notes: ajīrṇa may mean eating while the previous meal is undigested, or undigested (unwholesome) food; saṅkīrṇa 'mixed' (of incompatible items). Worm head disease is described in units 27-29.

words.gloss: of the one of evil deeds

hindi: तब सिर में क्लेद से उस पापकर्मी के कृमि ऐसा शिरोरोग उत्पन्न करते हैं जिसमें घृणित लक्षण उत्पन्न हो चुके हों।
english: Then, from the excess moisture (saṃkleda) in the head, worms of the evil-doer produce a head disease in which repulsive signs have arisen.

text_flags.why: possible spacing error: jāta has no case ending and can only stand as the first member of the compound jāta-bībhatsa-lakṣaṇam ('with repulsive signs arisen'); the syllable count is unchanged

notes: pāpakarmaṇaḥ is genitive singular: the worms 'of' the person of evil deeds (the patient).

words.gloss: distressed by piercing, cutting pain, itching, swelling and misery
words.gram: m. acc. sg., tat-puruṣa with dvandva

hindi: वेधने और काटने की पीड़ा, खुजली, सूजन और दुर्गति से दुःखी व्यक्ति को, और कृमियों के दिखने से, कृमिरोग से पीड़ित जानना चाहिए।
english: One should know (the person) distressed by piercing and cutting pain, itching, swelling and misery as afflicted with worm disease, and (know it) also by the sight of worms.
notes: vyadha-cheda-rujā may be 'pain of piercing and cutting' or 'piercing, cutting and pain'. daurgatya is read as printed ('misery, wretched state'). śopha = swelling (glossary).

words.gloss: by grief, fasting, exercise, and dry, withered and scanty food

hindi: शोक, उपवास, व्यायाम, रूखे, सूखे और थोड़े भोजन से वायु हृदय में प्रवेश करके अत्यन्त पीड़ा उत्पन्न करती है।
english: By grief, fasting, exercise (vyāyāma), and dry, withered and scanty food, Vāta (vāyu), having entered the heart, produces extreme pain.
notes: Heart diseases (units 30-40).

hindi: काँपना, ऐंठन, जकड़न, मूढ़ता, शून्यता और भय, यह वात से पीड़ित के हृदय में रूप है; और भोजन पच जाने पर अत्यधिक वेदना होती है।
english: Trembling, constriction (veṣṭana), stiffness, stupor, emptiness and fear: these are the symptoms in the heart of one afflicted by Vāta; and when (food) is digested, extreme pain.
notes: jīrṇe is read as a locative absolute, 'when (the meal) is digested'; the word 'food' is understood. dara may also mean 'fissure, tearing'; 'fear' is taken here.

words.gloss: by hot, sour, salty, alkali, pungent (food) and eating while undigested

hindi: उष्ण, अम्ल, लवण, क्षार, कटु भोजन और अजीर्ण में भोजन से, तथा मद्य, क्रोध और धूप से, हृदय में पित्त शीघ्र कुपित हो जाता है।
english: By hot, sour, salty, alkali (kṣāra) and pungent food and eating while undigested, and by wine, anger and sun, Pitta is quickly aggravated in the heart.

hindi: वात आदि के, रस आदि के, मलों के तथा ओज के क्षय (होते हैं); उनमें अनिल आदि के क्षय का लक्षण कहा जा चुका है।
english: (There are) decreases of Vāta and the rest, of rasa and the rest, of the wastes, and likewise of ojas; among them, the sign of decrease of Vāta (anila) and the rest has been stated.
notes: No verb in line 1; "there are" is understood (supplied in brackets). rasa here is the first of the bodily dhātus (rasa, blood, flesh ... as listed in units 64-69), not taste.

words.gloss: of one with very slight exertion

hindi: रस के क्षय में, बहुत थोड़ी चेष्टा करने वाले का भी हृदय क्षुब्ध होता है, ऊँचा शब्द नहीं सहता, धड़कता है, पीड़ित होता है और क्लान्त हो जाता है।
english: In the decrease of rasa, the heart of one even with very slight exertion is agitated, does not bear loud sound, palpitates, aches and becomes faint.
notes: The negative "na" printed after śabdam is construed with sahate ("does not bear loud sound"); read with dravati it would give "does not run (beat) strongly". dravati (literally "runs") is rendered "palpitates". svalpa = su + alpa.

words.gloss: wasting of buttocks, neck and abdomen
words.gram: f. nom. sg. tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: रक्त के क्षय में त्वचा कठोर, फटी हुई, मुरझाई हुई और रूखी होती है; मांस के क्षय में विशेष रूप से नितम्ब, गर्दन और उदर का सूखना (होता है)।
english: In the decrease of blood the skin is rough, cracked, faded and dry; in the decrease of flesh there is especially dryness of the buttocks, neck and abdomen.

text_flags.why: "puruṣā" (from puruṣa "man") gives no sense as a feminine adjective of tvak; paruṣā "rough" fits the series of f. adjectives (sphuṭitā, mlānā, rūkṣā) and keeps the metre. Possible typo.

hindi: जोड़ों का चटकना, ग्लानि, आँखों का श्रम और उदर का पतलापन, ये मेद के क्षीण होने पर लक्षण हैं।
english: Cracking of the joints, languor, strain of the eyes and thinness of the abdomen are the sign when fat (medas) is decreased.
notes: akṣṇoḥ may be construed with glāniḥ ("languor of the eyes") instead of with āyāsaḥ; the rendering takes it with āyāsaḥ.
lines_deva: लक्षणं मेदसि क्षीणे तनुत्वं चोदरस्य च
lines_iast: lakṣaṇaṃ medasi kṣīṇe tanutvaṃ codarasya ca

words.gloss: falling of head-hair, body-hair, nails, beard and teeth
words.gram: n. nom. sg. tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: केश, रोम, नख, दाढ़ी और दाँतों का गिरना, श्रम और जोड़ों की शिथिलता, इन्हें अस्थि के क्षय में लक्षण जानना चाहिए।
english: Falling of the head-hair, body-hair, nails, beard and teeth, fatigue, and looseness of the joints as well, are to be known as the sign in the decrease of bone.
notes: dvija ("twice-born") here means tooth.

words.gram: n. nom. pl. -in possessive of vāta-roga (tat-puruṣa)

hindi: मज्जा के क्षीण होने पर देहधारियों की अस्थियाँ मानो टूट-टूटकर गिरती हैं, और वे दुर्बल, हल्की तथा निरन्तर वात-रोगों से युक्त होती हैं।
english: When marrow is decreased, the bones of embodied beings crumble as it were, and are weak, light and constantly afflicted with Vāta diseases.
lines_deva: शीर्यन्त इव चास्थीनि दुर्बलानि लघूनि च
lines_iast: śīryanta iva cāsthīni durbalāni laghūni ca

words.gloss: of one whose semen is decreased

hindi: दुर्बलता, मुख का सूखना, पाण्डुता, शिथिलता, श्रम, नपुंसकता और शुक्र का न निकलना, ये क्षीण शुक्र वाले का लक्षण हैं।
english: Weakness, dryness of the mouth, pallor, lassitude (sadana), fatigue, impotence and non-emission of semen are the sign of one whose semen (śukra) is decreased.

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. part. caus. ud-√nam

hindi: शकृत् के क्षीण होने पर मारुत मानो आँतों को दबाता हुआ और रूखे व्यक्ति की कुक्षि को ऊपर उठाता हुआ तिरछा और ऊपर की ओर जाता है।
english: When faeces (śakṛt) are decreased, Vāta (māruta), as if squeezing the intestines and lifting up the belly of the dry person, moves sideways and upward.

text_flags.why: The Devanagari has ह् (h with virama) instead of visarga; m. nom. sg. mārutaḥ is required as subject.
kukṣi is an i-stem; the acc. sg. is kukṣim with short i. Possible typo (metre unaffected because the syllable is heavy either way).

notes: The ca of line 1 joins the two participles pīḍayan and unnamayan.

hindi: मूत्र के क्षय में मूत्रकृच्छ्र और मूत्र का विवर्ण होना होता है; उसको प्यास सताती है और उसका मुख सूख जाता है।
english: In the decrease of urine there is mūtrakṛcchra and discolouration of the urine as well; thirst afflicts him and his mouth dries up.

text_flags.why: The word kṛcchra is spelled with cch; the printed "kṛchra" lacks one c. Possible typo.
"pīāsā" is not a Sanskrit form; pipāsā "thirst" fits the sense and the subject of bādhate; the syllable count is 8 either way. Possible typo.

lines_iast: pīāsā bādhate cāsya mukhaṃ ca pariśuṣyati

hindi: और मल के क्षय में अन्य मलायन भी अपने-अपने अनुसार खाली, हल्के और सूखे हुए दिखाई देते हैं।
english: And in the decrease of waste, the other channels of waste are seen to be empty, light and dried up, each according to its own.

lines_iast: malāyanāni cānyāni śūnyāni ca laghūni ca

hindi: ओज के क्षय में (व्यक्ति) दुर्बल होकर बार-बार डरता है, चिन्ता करता है, उसकी इन्द्रियाँ व्यथित रहती हैं, उसकी कान्ति बुरी, मन उदास होता है, और वह रूखा तथा कृश होता है।
english: In the decrease of ojas, (the person) being weak fears constantly, broods, has afflicted senses, is of poor complexion, dejected, dry and emaciated as well.
notes: durbalaḥ may also be read as a separate predicate ("is weak"). chāyā is rendered "complexion".

hindi: जो शुद्ध, लाल और थोड़े पीलेपन से युक्त (पदार्थ) हृदय में स्थित रहता है, वह शरीर में ओज कहा गया है; उसके नाश से मनुष्य नष्ट हो जाता है।
english: That which abides in the heart, pure, red and slightly yellowish, is reckoned as ojas in the body; from its destruction a man perishes.
notes: raktam may also be read as a noun ("blood") with śuddham ("pure blood"), but the series of colour words supports "red". nā is the nom. sg. of nṛ "man".

words.gloss: having the smell of parched grain

hindi: देहधारियों के इस शरीर में वस्तुतः सबसे पहले ओज उत्पन्न होता है; वह घी के रंग वाला, मधु के रस वाला और लाजा की गन्ध वाला उत्पन्न होता है।
english: In this body of embodied beings ojas is indeed the first to be born; it arises having the colour of ghee, the taste of honey and the smell of parched grain (lāja).
notes: madhurasam is divided madhu-rasam ("having the taste of honey"). hi is rendered "indeed".

hindi: जैसे भौंरे फलों और फूलों से मधु इकट्ठा करते हैं, वैसे ही मनुष्यों का ओज गुणों द्वारा उनके अपने कर्मों से इकट्ठा किया जाता है।
english: Just as honey is gathered by bees from fruits and flowers, so the ojas of men is gathered by the qualities from their own actions.

text_flags.why: "sdaṃbhiryate" is not a form; line 2 of the same verse has saṃbhriyate in the parallel clause (yathā ... tadvat), which fits sense and metre.

notes: The input prints this verse in parentheses, with its own dandas inside the brackets and no verse number (numbered 75.1 here); the input does not say why. The Hindi uses an active construction for the passive of line 1.

words.gram: n. nom. sg. karmadhāraya (dvandva of adjectives first)

hindi: व्यायाम, उपवास, चिन्ता, रूखा, थोड़ा और नपा-तुला भोजन, हवा और धूप, भय, शोक, रूखा पान, जागरण,
english: Exercise, fasting, anxiety, dry, scanty and restricted eating, wind and sun, fear, grief, dry drinks, keeping awake,
notes: The list continues into unit 77 (predicate kṣayahetavaḥ). vāta here is the physical wind, not the doṣa.

hindi: कफ, रक्त, शुक्र और मलों का अत्यधिक निकलना, काल और भूतों द्वारा उपघात, इन्हें क्षय के कारण जानना चाहिए।
english: excessive discharge of Kapha, blood, semen and the wastes, time (kāla), and affliction by bhūtas, are to be known as the causes of decrease.
notes: Continues unit 76. bhūta is left as "bhūtas"; it can mean spirits or living beings, and the verse does not decide. ativartana is literally "going beyond", rendered "excessive discharge".

words.gloss: heavy, unctuous, sour and salty things

words.gram: m. gen. pl. pres. part. sam-√aś

hindi: जो भारी, स्निग्ध, खट्टे और नमकीन पदार्थ अत्यधिक मात्रा में खाते हैं, तथा नया अन्न और (नया) पान, निद्रा और बैठने के सुखों का सेवन करते हैं,
english: In those who partake in excess of heavy, unctuous, sour and salty things, of new grain and drink, of sleep and the comforts of sitting,
notes: The sentence continues into unit 79. samaśnatām ("eating") governs all the accusatives; with sleep and comforts it is rendered "partake of". navam may qualify pānam as well as annam.

words.gloss: of those who have given up exercise and thought

words.gram: m. gen. pl. pres. part. neg. √kṛ

hindi: जिन्होंने व्यायाम और चिन्तन छोड़ दिया है और जो संशोधन नहीं करते, उनमें श्लेष्मा, पित्त, मेद और मांस अत्यधिक बढ़ जाते हैं।
english: who have given up exercise and thought, and who do not undergo purification (saṃśodhana), Kapha (śleṣman), Pitta, fat and flesh increase excessively.
notes: Continues unit 78. The verb is singular with four subjects. cintā is rendered "thought" here (in unit 76, where it is a cause of decrease, "anxiety").
lines_deva: श्लेष्मा पित्तं च मेदश्च मांसं चातिप्रवर्धते
lines_iast: śleṣmā pittaṃ ca medaśca māṃsaṃ cātipravardhate

hindi: जब उनसे जिसकी गति रुक गई है, ऐसा वायु ओज को लेकर बस्ति में जाता है, तब कठिन मधुमेह प्रवृत्त होता है।
english: When Vāta (vāyu), its movement obstructed by them, takes the ojas and goes to the bladder (basti), then madhumeha, which is difficult, sets in.
notes: kṛcchra is rendered "difficult" (that is, hard to treat); the verse does not say more. madhumeha is kept as Sanskrit.
lines_deva: यदा बस्तिं तदा कृच्छ्रो मधुमेहः प्रवर्तते
lines_iast: yadā bastiṃ tadā kṛcchro madhumehaḥ pravartate

hindi: वह बार-बार मारुत, पित्त और कफ का स्वरूप दिखाता है, और क्षय को प्राप्त होकर फिर बढ़ जाता है।
english: It shows again and again the form of Vāta (māruta), Pitta and Kapha; having gone into decline, it swells again.
notes: "It" (saḥ) is taken as madhumeha from unit 80.
lines_deva: स मारुतस्य पित्तस्य कफस्य च मुहुर्मुहुः
lines_iast: sa mārutasya pittasya kaphasya ca muhurmuhuḥ

hindi: इसकी उपेक्षा से मांसल स्थानों में, मर्मों में और सन्धियों में भी सात दारुण पिडकाएँ उत्पन्न होती हैं।
english: Through neglect of it, seven harsh boils (piḍakā) arise in fleshy places, and in the vital points (marma) and joints as well.
notes: asya is taken as madhumeha.

hindi: शराविका, कच्छपिका, जालिनी, सर्षपी, अलजी, विनता नाम की और सातवीं विद्रधी।
english: Śarāvikā, Kacchapikā, Jālinī, Sarṣapī, Alajī, the one called Vinatā, and Vidradhī as the seventh.
notes: The names are kept as names; the verse gives no descriptions here.
lines_deva: अलजी विनताख्या च विद्रधी चेति सप्तमी
lines_iast: alajī vinatākhyā ca vidradhī ceti saptamī

words.gloss: having the shape of a shallow dish

hindi: जो पिडका किनारों पर उठी हुई, बीच में धँसी हुई, श्याव वर्ण की, क्लेद और पीड़ा से युक्त और शराव के आकार में स्थित हो, वह शराविका होती है।
english: An eruption (piḍakā) that is raised at the edges, depressed in the middle, dusky, accompanied by moisture and pain, and shaped like a shallow dish (śarāva) would be śarāvikā.
notes: ruganvitā = ruj + anvitā (j becomes g before a vowel). śarāva is a shallow earthen dish; the name śarāvikā is derived from it.

hindi: गहरी पीड़ा और चुभन वाली, बड़े स्थान को घेरने वाली, चिकनी, कछुए की पीठ जैसी पिडका कच्छपी मानी गई है।
english: An eruption with deep pain and pricking, occupying a large site, smooth, resembling the back of a tortoise, is considered kacchapī.
notes: kacchapī here is the eruption called kacchapikā in the list of unit 83 and in unit 105. avagāḍha may also be read as "deep-seated" qualifying the eruption itself; the compound is taken as "deep pain and pricking".

hindi: जकड़ी हुई, शिराओं के जाल वाली, चिकने स्राव वाली, बड़े आशय वाली, पीड़ा और चुभन से भरी और सूक्ष्म छिद्रों वाली जालिनी है।
english: Stiff, with a network of vessels, with an unctuous discharge, with a large base, abounding in pain and pricking, and with fine openings, is jālinī.
notes: The word piḍakā is not repeated in this verse; the subject is jālinī. mahāśayā: āśaya "seat, base"; it may also mean "deep-seated".

hindi: जो पिडका बहुत बड़ी न हो, शीघ्र पकने वाली और अत्यधिक पीड़ा वाली हो, तथा सरसों जैसी पिडकाओं से व्याप्त हो, वह सर्षपी होती है।
english: An eruption that is not very large, quickly suppurating and very painful, covered with eruptions resembling mustard seeds (sarṣapa), would be sarṣapī.
notes: The printed token nātimahatīkṣiprapākā runs together two words (nātimahatī and kṣiprapākā); the split keeps both in this one token. sarṣapa = mustard seed (standard).

words.gram: f. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: अलजी उत्पन्न होने पर त्वचा को जलाती है, तृष्णा, मोह और ज्वर उत्पन्न करती है, निरन्तर फैलती है और अग्नि की तरह कष्टपूर्वक जलाती है।
english: Alajī burns the skin at its arising, causes thirst, confusion (moha) and fever, spreads incessantly, and burns painfully like fire.
notes: duḥkhāt is taken adverbially ("painfully"); it may also mean "with distress" to the patient. moha may also be rendered "fainting".

hindi: पीठ पर या उदर पर होने वाली, गहरी पीड़ा और क्लेद वाली, बड़ी, धँसी हुई और नीली पिडका विनता मानी गई है।
english: An eruption on the back or on the abdomen, with deep pain and moisture, large, depressed and bluish, is considered vinatā.
notes: The first vinatā is the participle "bent down, depressed"; the second is the name of the eruption, which plays on it.
lines_deva: महती विनता नीला पिडका विनता मता
lines_iast: mahatī vinatā nīlā piḍakā vinatā matā

words.gloss: arising from skin, sinew and flesh
words.gram: f. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: विद्रधि को दो प्रकार की कहते हैं: बाह्य और आभ्यन्तर। बाह्य विद्रधि त्वचा, स्नायु और मांस से उत्पन्न, कण्डरा के समान और अत्यधिक पीड़ा वाली होती है।
english: They declare vidradhi (abscess) to be of two kinds, external and internal. The external one arises from skin, sinew and flesh, resembles a kaṇḍarā (tendon) and is very painful.
notes: kaṇḍarābhā "resembling a kaṇḍarā" is taken as describing its shape; the exact point of comparison is not stated. Units 91 to 95 describe the internal vidradhi.

words.gloss: from excessive eating of cold food and of burning, hot, dry and dried things
words.gram: n. abl. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first members)

words.gloss: from eating incompatible, undigested, spoiled, irregular and unsuitable food
words.gram: n. abl. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first members)

hindi: ठण्डे अन्न, विदाही, उष्ण, रूक्ष और सूखे पदार्थों के अति भोजन से; विरुद्ध, अजीर्ण, दूषित, विषम और असात्म्य भोजन से;
english: From excessive eating of cold food and of burning (vidāhin), hot, dry and dried things; from eating incompatible, undigested, spoiled, irregular and unsuitable food;
notes: The sentence runs from unit 91 to unit 93. ati- in the first line may qualify all the preceding items ("excessive eating of ...") or stand as a separate item "overeating". ajīrṇa may mean eating while the previous meal is undigested. śītaka is taken as "cold"; it may also mean "stale".

words.gloss: from spoiled wine and much wine

words.gram: n. abl. sg., karmadhāraya (dvandva second members)

words.gloss: from excessive load, walking and sexual intercourse
words.gram: n. abl. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva second members)

hindi: बिगड़े हुए और अधिक मद्य के सेवन से, वेगों को रोकने से, श्रम से, टेढ़े ढंग के व्यायाम और शयन से, अति भार, मार्ग-गमन और मैथुन से,
english: from spoiled wine (madya) and much wine, from suppression of urges (vega), from fatigue, from crooked exercise and lying, and from excess of loads, walking and sexual intercourse,
notes: vyāpannabahumadyatva is literally "the state of (having) spoiled and much wine". jihma "crooked" is taken with both exercise and lying (improper postures). ati is taken with load, walking and sexual intercourse.

hindi: जब मल शरीर के भीतर मांस और रक्त में प्रवेश करते हैं, तब गहराई में स्थित, अत्यन्त दारुण ग्रन्थि उत्पन्न होती है,
english: when the wastes (mala) enter the flesh and blood inside the body, then a deep-seated, very harsh swelling (granthi) arises,
notes: malāḥ is rendered by the fixed rendering "wastes (mala)"; in this context the word refers to the vitiated substances that enter flesh and blood. The sentence continues into unit 94.

hindi: हृदय, क्लोम, यकृत्, प्लीहा, कुक्षि और दोनों वृक्कों में, नाभि में, या दोनों वंक्षणों में, अथवा बस्ति में, तीव्र वेदना वाली।
english: in the heart, the kloman, the liver, the spleen, the kukṣi (abdomen) and the two kidneys, in the navel, or in the two groins, or in the bladder (basti), with intense pain.
notes: tīvravedanaḥ agrees with granthiḥ of unit 93. kloman is kept in Sanskrit; its identification is disputed.
lines_deva: हृदये क्लोम्नि यकृति प्लीह्नि कुक्षौ च वृक्कयोः
lines_iast: hṛdaye klomni yakṛti plīhni kukṣau ca vṛkkayoḥ

words.gloss: because of the excess of vitiated blood

hindi: दूषित रक्त की अधिकता के कारण वह वस्तुतः शीघ्र विदग्ध होती है; इसलिए शीघ्र विदग्ध होने के कारण उसे विद्रधि कहा जाता है।
english: Because of the excess of vitiated blood it is indeed quickly burnt (vidahyate); therefore, because it burns quickly, it is called vidradhī.
notes: The verse explains the name vidradhī from vi-√dah "to burn, become inflamed". saḥ (masculine) refers to granthiḥ of unit 93, while vidradhī is feminine.

words.gloss: by piercing, cutting, giddiness, distension, sound, throbbing and creeping
by thirst, burning, confusion, intoxication and fever

hindi: वेधने, काटने, भ्रम, आनाह, शब्द, फड़कन और रेंगने से वातिक विद्रधि को, तृष्णा, दाह, मोह, मद और ज्वर से पैत्तिक को,
english: By piercing, cutting, giddiness, distension (ānāha), sound, throbbing and creeping, the Vāta type; by thirst, burning, confusion (moha), intoxication (mada) and fever, the Pitta type;
notes: The verb viduḥ "they know" is in unit 97 and governs vātikīm, paittikīm and ślaiṣmikīm. bhrama may also mean "a whirling sensation" here.

words.gloss: by yawning, nausea, loss of taste, stiffness and coldness

hindi: और जम्हाई, उत्क्लेश, अरुचि, जकड़न और शीतलता से श्लैष्मिक को जानते हैं। और सभी विद्रधियों में बड़ा शूल उत्पन्न होता है।
english: and by yawning, nausea (utkleśa), loss of taste (aruci), stiffness and coldness they know the Kapha type. And in all vidradhīs great pain (śūla) arises.
notes: śītaka is taken as "coldness, feeling cold".

hindi: खट्टेपन की अवस्था को प्राप्त विद्रधि मानो शस्त्रों और अस्त्रों से भेदी जाती है, मानो जलती लकड़ियों से जलाई जाती है, और मानो बिच्छुओं से डसी जाती है।
english: A vidradhī that has reached souring (vyamlatā) is as if split by weapons and missiles, as if burnt by firebrands, and as if stung by scorpions.

text_flags.why: possible: yātā ("having gone to") needs an accusative of the state reached; the nominative vyamlatā gives no construction. The metre (8 syllables) is the same either way.

notes: vidradhī is taken as the subject of all three passive verbs; the first line may also describe what the patient feels. vyamlatā (from vi-amla "turned sour") is the souring stage of the swelling.

words.gloss: resembling the water of tila, māṣa and kulattha
words.gram: n. acc. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first members)

hindi: वातविद्रधि पतला, रूक्ष, अरुण, श्याव और झागदार (स्राव बहाती है); पित्तविद्रधि तिल, माष और कुलत्थ के जल जैसा,
english: The Vāta vidradhī (discharges) a thin, rough, reddish, dusky and frothy (fluid); the Pitta vidradhī, one resembling the water of tila, māṣa and kulattha;
notes: The verb sravati is in unit 100 and is understood here; the neuter accusatives describe the discharge. uda = udaka "water" in compounds. tila = sesame (standard); māṣa = black gram (standard); kulattha = horse gram (standard).

words.gloss: the one from all doṣas combined

hindi: श्लैष्मिक विद्रधि सफेद, पिच्छिल, गाढ़ा और बहुत स्राव बहाती है; सान्निपातिक विद्रधि ये सभी लक्षण धारण करती है।
english: The Kapha type discharges a white, slimy, thick fluid, copiously; the sānnipātikī (from all the doṣas combined) takes on all these signs.
notes: lakṣaṇam is singular in form but collective ("all this set of signs").
lines_deva: श्लैष्मिकी स्रवति श्वेतं पिच्छिलं बहलं बहु
lines_iast: ślaiṣmikī sravati śvetaṃ picchilaṃ bahalaṃ bahu

words.gloss: for knowing the distinction of curability and incurability
arising in the chief vital point
jolting of the heart, tamaka, stupor, cough and dyspnoea
in one arising in the kloman
thirst, dryness of the mouth and catching of the throat
in one arising in the liver
in one arising in the spleen
in one arising in the kukṣi
pain in the kukṣi, sides and between the shoulders
words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first members)

words.gloss: in one arising in the kidney
in one arising in the navel
in one arising in the groin
in one arising in the bladder
difficult and foul-smelling urine and faeces

hindi: अब इन विद्रधियों की साध्यता और असाध्यता के भेद को जानने के लिए हम स्थान के कारण होने वाले लक्षणों के भेद का उपदेश करेंगे। वहाँ प्रधान मर्म में उत्पन्न विद्रधि में हृदय में धक्का-सा लगना, तमक, प्रमोह, कास और श्वास होते हैं; क्लोम में उत्पन्न में प्यास, मुख का सूखना और गले का जकड़ना; यकृत् में उत्पन्न में श्वास; प्लीहा में उत्पन्न में उच्छ्वास का रुकना; कुक्षि में उत्पन्न में कुक्षि, पार्श्व और कन्धों के बीच शूल; वृक्क में उत्पन्न में पीठ और कमर की जकड़न; नाभि में उत्पन्न में हिक्का; वंक्षण में उत्पन्न में जाँघों की शिथिलता; और बस्ति में उत्पन्न में कष्ट से और दुर्गन्धयुक्त मूत्र और मल का होना।
english: Now, for knowing the distinction between the curability and incurability of these vidradhīs, we shall teach the distinction of signs caused by location. There, in a vidradhī arising in the chief vital point (marma): jolting of the heart, tamaka, stupor (pramoha), cough and dyspnoea; in one arising in the kloman: thirst, dryness of the mouth and catching of the throat; in one arising in the liver: dyspnoea; in one arising in the spleen: obstruction of breathing; in one arising in the kukṣi: pain in the kukṣi, the sides and between the shoulders; in one arising in the kidney: stiffness of the back and waist; in one arising in the navel: hiccup; in one arising in the groin: weakness of the thighs; and in one arising in the bladder: difficult and foul-smelling urine and faeces.
notes: A prose passage although it is numbered as a verse unit. The chief vital point (pradhāna marma) is listed where unit 94 has hṛdaya (heart); its symptoms begin with the heart. tamaka is kept in Sanskrit. The token "---" is the printed dash.
lines_deva: अथासां विद्रधीनां साध्यासाध्यत्वविशेषज्ञानार्थं स्थानकृतं लिङ्गविशेषमुपदेक्ष्यामः --- तत्र प्रधानमर्मजायां विद्रध्यां हृद्घट्टनतमकप्रमोहकासश्वासाः, क्लोमजायां पिपासामुखशोषगलग्रहाः, यकृज्जायां श्वासः, प्लीहजायामुच्छ्वासोपरोधः, कुक्षिजायां कुक्षिपार्श्वान्तरांसशूलं, वृक्कजायां पृष्ठकटिग्रहः, नाभिजायां हिक्का, वंक्षणजायां सक्थिसादः, बस्तिजायां कृच्छ्रपूतिमूत्रवर्चस्त्वं चेति
lines_iast: athāsāṃ vidradhīnāṃ sādhyāsādhyatvaviśeṣajñānārthaṃ sthānakṛtaṃ liṅgaviśeṣamupadekṣyāmaḥ --- tatra pradhānamarmajāyāṃ vidradhyāṃ hṛdghaṭṭanatamakapramohakāsaśvāsāḥ, klomajāyāṃ pipāsāmukhaśoṣagalagrahāḥ, yakṛjjāyāṃ śvāsaḥ, plīhajāyāmucchvāsoparodhaḥ, kukṣijāyāṃ kukṣipārśvāntarāṃsaśūlaṃ, vṛkkajāyāṃ pṛṣṭhakaṭigrahaḥ, nābhijāyāṃ hikkā, vaṃkṣaṇajāyāṃ sakthisādaḥ, bastijāyāṃ kṛcchrapūtimūtravarcastvaṃ ceti

words.gloss: in those arising in the navel

hindi: पककर फूट जाने पर ऊपर उत्पन्न होने वाली विद्रधियों में स्राव मुख से बहता है, नीचे उत्पन्न होने वालियों में गुदा से, और नाभि में उत्पन्न होने वालियों में दोनों ओर से।
english: When they have ripened and burst, in those arising above the discharge flows from the mouth, in those arising below from the anus, but in those arising in the navel from both.
notes: Prose numbered as a verse unit.
lines_deva: पक्वप्रभिन्नासूर्ध्वजासु मुखात् स्रावः स्रवति, अधोजासु गुदात्, उभयतस्तु नाभिजासु
lines_iast: pakvaprabhinnāsūrdhvajāsu mukhāt srāvaḥ sravati, adhojāsu gudāt, ubhayatastu nābhijāsu

words.gloss: arising in heart, navel and bladder
words.gram: f. nom. pl., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first members)

words.gloss: the one from all doṣas combined

hindi: इनमें से हृदय, नाभि और बस्ति में उत्पन्न होने वाली, पूरी तरह पक जाने पर, और सान्निपातिक विद्रधि मृत्यु के लिए होती हैं; शेष तो कुशल और शीघ्र उपचार करने वाले चिकित्सक को पाकर शान्त हो जाती हैं।
english: Of these, those arising in the heart, navel and bladder when fully ripened, and the sānnipātikī one, are for death; the rest, however, subside on reaching a skilful physician who treats quickly.
notes: Prose numbered as a verse unit. paripakvāḥ may be read with the first group only (as rendered) or as applying also to the sānnipātikī one.
lines_deva: आसां हृन्नाभिबस्तिजाः परिपक्वाः सान्निपातिकी च मरणाय; शेषाः पुनः कुशलमाशुप्रतिकारिणं चिकित्सकमासाद्योपशाम्यन्ति
lines_iast: āsāṃ hṛnnābhibastijāḥ paripakvāḥ sānnipātikī ca maraṇāya; śeṣāḥ punaḥ kuśalamāśupratikāriṇaṃ cikitsakamāsādyopaśāmyanti

words.gloss: like a weapon, a snake, lightning and fire
words.gram: f. acc. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first members)

hindi: इसलिए शस्त्र, सर्प, बिजली और अग्नि के समान, अभी-अभी उत्पन्न हुई विद्रधि का स्नेह और विरेचन से शीघ्र ही उपचार करे, और सब प्रकार से गुल्म के समान।
english: Therefore one should treat a recently arisen vidradhī, which is like a weapon, a snake, lightning and fire, right away with unctuous substances (sneha) and purgation (virecana), and in every way as for gulma.
notes: gulmavat "like gulma": the vidradhī is to be treated in every way as gulma is treated.
lines_deva: तस्मादचिरोत्थितां विद्रधीं शस्त्रसर्पविद्युदग्नितुल्यां स्नेहविरेचनैराश्वेवोपक्रमेत् सर्वशो गुल्मवच्चेति
lines_iast: tasmādacirotthitāṃ vidradhīṃ śastrasarpavidyudagnitulyāṃ snehavirecanairāśvevopakramet sarvaśo gulmavacceti

words.gloss: of one whose fat (medas) is vitiated

hindi: और यहाँ हैं: ये पिडकाएँ प्रमेह के बिना भी दूषित मेद वाले व्यक्ति में उत्पन्न होती हैं, और जब तक स्थान का ग्रहण न हो, तब तक ये दिखाई नहीं देतीं।
english: And here there are: These arise even without prameha in one whose fat (medas) is vitiated, and they are not noticed until there is occupation of a site.
notes: duṣṭamedasaḥ may also be a feminine nominative plural bahuvrīhi agreeing with etāḥ ("having vitiated fat"). The construction tāvat ... na ... yāvat is rendered "not ... until"; vāstuparigraha refers to the eruptions taking up a site, as in unit 85.

words.gloss: of one with abundant Kapha and fat
words.gram: m. gen. sg., bahuvrīhi (dvandva second members)

hindi: शराविका, कच्छपिका और जालिनी दुःसह हैं, क्योंकि वे प्रचुर श्लेष्मा और मेद वाले व्यक्ति में अत्यन्त बलवान होकर उत्पन्न होती हैं।
english: Śarāvikā, kacchapikā and jālinī are hard to bear, for they arise very strong in one with abundant Kapha (śleṣman) and fat.
notes: prabhūtaśleṣmamedasaḥ may also be a feminine nominative plural bahuvrīhi agreeing with tāḥ ("having abundant Kapha and fat"), as in unit 104.

hindi: और जो सर्षपी, अलजी, विनता और विद्रधि हैं, वे साध्य और पित्त की प्रबलता वाली हैं; वे अल्प मेद वाले व्यक्ति में उत्पन्न होती हैं।
english: Those that are sarṣapī, alajī, vinatā and vidradhī are curable and Pitta-predominant; they, however, arise in one with little fat.
notes: sādhyāḥ and pittolbaṇāḥ may be read either inside the relative clause (as in the English) or as the predicate of tāḥ.
lines_deva: सर्षपी चालजी चैव विनता विद्रधी च याः
lines_iast: sarṣapī cālajī caiva vinatā vidradhī ca yāḥ

hindi: जिसके मर्मों में, कन्धे में, गुदा में, हाथों में, स्तन में, सन्धियों में और पैरों में पिडकाएँ उत्पन्न होती हैं, वह प्रमेही जीवित नहीं रहता।
english: The prameha patient in whom eruptions arise in the vital points (marma), the shoulder, the anus, the hands, the breast, the joints and the feet does not live.

text_flags.why: the lone "a" is not a word; the relative yasya needs the correlative saḥ (sa) with pramehī, and "sa" keeps the 8 syllables of the pāda. The Devanagari line also prints अ.

lines_deva: मर्मस्वंसे गुदे पाण्योः स्तने सन्धिषु पादयोः
जायन्ते यस्य पिडकाः अ प्रमेही न जीवति
lines_iast: marmasvaṃse gude pāṇyoḥ stane sandhiṣu pādayoḥ
jāyante yasya piḍakāḥ a pramehī na jīvati

hindi: इसी प्रकार अन्य पिडकाएँ हैं: लाल, पीली, काली, अरुण, पाण्डुर, पाण्डु वर्ण की, राख जैसी और गहरी नीली आभा वाली।
english: Likewise there are other eruptions: red, yellow, black, reddish, whitish, pale-coloured, ash-like, and with a dark-blue lustre.
notes: bhasmābhā stands for bhasmābhāḥ (visarga dropped after ā before a voiced sound). The colour words are read as a list of different eruptions; the sentence continues into unit 109.

hindi: कुछ कोमल हैं और अन्य कठोर, कुछ बड़ी और इसी प्रकार अन्य छोटी, कुछ मन्द वेग वाली, कुछ तीव्र वेग वाली, कुछ बहुत थोड़े शूल वाली और कुछ अत्यधिक पीड़ा वाली।
english: some soft and others hard, some large and likewise others small, some slow in course, some rapid in course, some with very little pain, some with great pain.
notes: vega here means the force or speed of the eruption, not an urge. mandavegā and svalpaśūlā stand for -vegāḥ and -śūlāḥ (visarga dropped after ā before a voiced sound). "some" in the translation renders the contrast anyāḥ / aparāḥ.

hindi: उन्हें अपने-अपने हेतुओं और लक्षणों से मारुत आदि की जानकर, उपद्रव दिखाई देने से पहले, उनका कथन करे और शीघ्र उपचार करे।
english: Having recognised them as of Vāta (māruta) and the others by their respective causes and signs, one should declare them and treat them quickly, before complications (upadrava) appear.
notes: mārutādīnām (genitive) is taken as "belonging to Vāta and the others"; it may also be read with hetulakṣaṇaiḥ ("by the respective causes and signs of Vāta and the others").

words.gloss: thirst, dyspnoea, putrefaction of flesh, confusion, hiccup, intoxication and fever
vīsarpa and obstruction of the vital points

hindi: तृष्णा, श्वास, मांस का सड़ना, मोह, हिक्का, मद, ज्वर, वीसर्प और मर्मों का अवरोध पिडकाओं के उपद्रव हैं।
english: Thirst, dyspnoea, putrefaction of the flesh, confusion (moha), hiccup, intoxication (mada), fever, vīsarpa and obstruction of the vital points (marma) are the complications (upadrava) of the eruptions.
notes: tṛṭ = tṛṣ "thirst" in compound form. marmasaṃrodha may also be "obstruction at the vital points".

hindi: क्षय, स्थान और वृद्धि, यह दोषों की तीन प्रकार की गति है; ऊपर, नीचे और तिरछी, यह दूसरी तीन प्रकार की गति जाननी चाहिए।
english: Diminution (kṣaya), stability (sthāna) and increase (vṛddhi) are the threefold course (gati) of the doṣas; upward, downward and sideways is to be known as another threefold one.
notes: sthāna here is the steady (normal) state between diminution and increase.
lines_deva: क्षयः स्थानं च वृद्धिश्च दोषाणां त्रिविधा गतिः
lines_iast: kṣayaḥ sthānaṃ ca vṛddhiśca doṣāṇāṃ trividhā gatiḥ

words.gloss: in the koṣṭha, the śākhās, and the vital points, bones and joints

hindi: और एक अन्य तीन प्रकार की गति कोष्ठ, शाखाओं तथा मर्म, अस्थि और सन्धियों में है। इस प्रकार विधि के भेद से दोषों की तीन प्रकार की गति कही गई।
english: And another threefold one is in the trunk (koṣṭha), the periphery (śākhā) and the vital points, bones and joints. Thus the threefold course of the doṣas has been stated by distinction of kind.
notes: The three sites are read as koṣṭha, śākhā, and marma-asthi-sandhi (vital points, bones and joints) taken together, which gives the three of trividhā.

words.gloss: beginning with the coming of clouds

hindi: पित्त आदि के चय, प्रकोप और प्रशम क्रम से, एक-एक करके, मेघों के आगमन से आरम्भ होने वाले छह कालों में होते हैं।
english: The accumulation, aggravation and pacification of Pitta and the others occur in order, one by one, in the six seasons beginning with the coming of the clouds.
notes: The token ekaikaśaḥṣaṭsu runs two words together without a space; the split keeps both in this one token.

hindi: और चय से आरम्भ होने वाली यह गति फिर कालकृत कही जाती है। और गति दो प्रकार की देखी गई है: जो प्राकृत है और जो वैकृत है।
english: And this course beginning with accumulation is further called the time-made (course). And the course is seen to be twofold: that which is natural (prākṛtī) and that which is morbid (vaikṛtī).
notes: punaḥ is rendered "further"; it may also mean "again".
lines_deva: गतिश्च द्विविधा दृष्टा प्राकृती वैकृती च या
lines_iast: gatiśca dvividhā dṛṣṭā prākṛtī vaikṛtī ca yā

hindi: मनुष्यों का पाक केवल ऊष्मा रूपी पित्त से होता है, और वह पित्त कुपित होकर बहुत से विकार उत्पन्न करता है।
english: Digestion (pakti) in men arises from Pitta alone, the heat (ūṣman); and that Pitta, when aggravated, produces many disorders (vikāra).
notes: ūṣmaṇaḥ is taken as ablative in apposition to pittāt ("from Pitta, the heat"); it may also be genitive ("the digestion of heat"). eva is restrictive and is rendered "alone".
lines_deva: तच्च पित्तं प्रकुपितं विकारान् कुरुते बहून्
lines_iast: tacca pittaṃ prakupitaṃ vikārān kurute bahūn

hindi: प्राकृत अवस्था में श्लेष्मा बल है और विकृत होने पर मल कहा जाता है; वही शरीर में ओज माना गया है और वह पाप्मा कहा जाता है।
english: But Kapha (śleṣman) in its normal state is strength, and when disordered is called waste (mala); that same (Kapha) is regarded as ojas (vital essence) in the body, and it is designated as evil (pāpman).
notes: mala stands for malaḥ (visarga dropped before u). ojas is glossed "vital essence" at first use in this chunk.
lines_deva: प्राकृतस्तु बलं श्लेष्मा विकृतो मल उच्यते
स चैवौजः स्मृतः काये स च पाप्मोपदिश्यते
lines_iast: prākṛtastu balaṃ śleṣmā vikṛto mala ucyate
sa caivaujaḥ smṛtaḥ kāye sa ca pāpmopadiśyate

hindi: क्योंकि सारी चेष्टा वात से होती है, वह प्राणियों का प्राण माना गया है; उसी से रोग उत्पन्न होते हैं और उसी से अवरोध होता है।
english: For all movement is by Vāta; it is regarded as the life-breath (prāṇa) of living beings. By that same (Vāta) diseases arise, and by it there is obstruction.
notes: The subject of uparudhyate is not stated; it may be life (prāṇa) or the person. The impersonal rendering "there is obstruction" keeps that open.
lines_deva: सर्वा हि चेष्टा वातेन स प्राणः प्राणिनां स्मृतः
lines_iast: sarvā hi ceṣṭā vātena sa prāṇaḥ prāṇināṃ smṛtaḥ

hindi: अपने आप को सदा निकट स्थित शत्रुओं वाला देखकर, अनश्वर आयु चाहने वाला आत्मवान् व्यक्ति सदा सावधान रहकर अपनी देखभाल करे।
english: Regarding himself as one whose enemies are always near at hand, the self-controlled man, wishing for a lasting life, should always attend to himself with care.
notes: paricaret has no stated object; "himself" is taken from ātmānam. anitvaram literally "not transient".

hindi: यहाँ दो श्लोक: हृदय रोगों के साथ सिर के रोग, मान के विकल्प से उत्पन्न होने वाले रोग, पिडकाओं के साथ क्षय, और दोषों की गति कही गई हैं,
english: Here, the two verses: The diseases of the head together with heart diseases, the diseases born of gradations of measure, the diminutions (kṣaya) together with the eruptions, and the course of the doṣas have been stated
notes: The summary sentence continues into unit 121, which gives the agent and the chapter. māna "measure" refers to the gradations of the doṣas described earlier in the chapter.

words.gloss: by one who sees the truth

hindi: इस कियन्तःशिरसीय अध्याय में, तत्त्वदर्शी और प्रजाओं के हित की इच्छा रखने वाले चिकित्सक द्वारा, ज्ञान के लिए।
english: in this Kiyantaḥśirasīya chapter, for the sake of knowledge, by the physician who sees the truth and desires the welfare of the people.
notes: The second line has 14 syllables where the metre expects 16; two syllables may be missing. The printed text is kept and nothing is restored. The placement of ca is taken as joining tattvadarśinā and hitaiṣiṇā.

hindi: इस प्रकार अग्निवेश द्वारा रचित, चरक द्वारा प्रतिसंस्कृत तन्त्र के श्लोकस्थान में कियन्तःशिरसीय नामक सत्रहवाँ अध्याय।
english: Thus, in the treatise composed by Agniveśa and redacted by Caraka, in the Śloka section (Ślokasthāna), the seventeenth chapter named Kiyantaḥśirasīya.
notes: Chapter colophon; the Sanskrit has no verb and the translation keeps it verbless.
lines_deva: इत्यग्निवेशकृते तन्त्रे चरकप्रतिसंस्कृते श्लोकस्थाने कियन्तःशिरसीयो नाम सप्तदशोऽध्यायः
lines_iast: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte ślokasthāne kiyantaḥśirasīyo nāma saptadaśo'dhyāyaḥ
